headline: Queen Guitarist Transforms Farmland Into Wildlife Haven
meta_description: Brian May's nature reserve has planted 100,000 trees across 157 acres of former farmland, creating habitat for wild animals.
summary_short: Queen's Brian May has converted 157 acres of empty farmland into a thriving nature reserve with 100,000 trees and wildlife habitat.
body:
Queen guitarist Brian May has transformed 157 acres of empty farmland into a flourishing nature reserve teeming with wild animals and newly planted trees. The project represents a significant commitment to rewilding and environmental restoration.

The reserve now supports approximately 100,000 trees across its expanse, fundamentally reshaping what was once barren agricultural land. By converting previously unused farmland into active wildlife habitat, the initiative demonstrates how private land stewardship can create meaningful ecological impact.

May's nature reserve stands as a tangible example of how musicians and public figures can leverage their resources toward environmental causes. The project bridges the gap between conservation ambition and ground-level restoration work, turning empty acreage into a living, breathing ecosystem for animals and plants alike.
